hints.content:
###Are $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{A'D'}$ on distinct parallel lines?

A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

[[☃ explanation 2]]

options.explanation:
Since dilations preserve angle measures, that includes the angle measure between a segment and the ray passing through the center of dilation and the endpoint of the segment.



[[☃ image 1]]

When corresponding angles formed by a transversal have the same measures, the lines the transversal intersects are parallel.

[Experiment in Desmos](https://www.desmos.com/geometry/8uiloai40g)

When both endpoints of a segment fall on the same ray from the center of dilation, the image of the segment is still on the same ray.



[[☃ image 2]]

[Experiment in Desmos](https://www.desmos.com/geometry/wbtgmsdtf1)

options.alt: A pre-image triangle Q R S and and image triangle Q prime R prime S prime where point S is labeled Center of Dilation. The pre-image triangle is inside of the image triangle where points Q and Q prime have congruent angles. Points R and R prime have congruent angles as well.

A point labeled center of dilation with a dashed ray extending from it. On the ray are the pre-image of line segment Q P and the image of line segment Q prime P prime. The pre-image line segment is closer to the center of dilation and is smaller than its image line segment.

hints.content: The line through $\overline{AD}$ does *not* pass through center $P$. So segments $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{A'D'}$ **are on distinct parallel lines**.

hints.content:
The line through $\overline{CD}$ doesn't pass through center $P$. So segments $\overline{CD}$ and $\overline{C'D'}$ are on parallel lines.

Since $\overline{CD}$ is perpendicular to the $x$-axis, that means $\overline{C'D'}$ **is also perpendicular to the $x$-axis**.

Claims about pre-image and image | True or false 
:- | :-:
$\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{A'D'}$ are on distinct parallel lines. | True
$\overline{CD}$ and $\overline{C'D'}$ are both perpendicular to the $x$-axis. | True

The pre-image Quadrilateral A B C D has point A at negative one, negative one, point B at zero, three, point C at two, one, and point D at two, zero. A point P is at negative four, negative three. The image Quadrilateral A prime B prime C prime D prime has point A prime at two, one, point B prime at four, nine, point C prime at eight, five, and point D prime at eight, negative five. A point P is at negative four, negative three.

question.content:
Quadrilateral $A'B'C'D'$ is the result of dilating quadrilateral $ABCD$ about point $P$ by a scale factor of $2$.


[[☃ image 1]]

**Determine whether each claim about the properties of $ABCD$ and $A'B'C'D'$ is true or false.**

 | | 
:- | :-:|
$\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{A'D'}$ are on distinct parallel lines. | [[☃ dropdown 1]]|
$\overline{CD}$ and $\overline{C'D'}$ are both perpendicular to the $x$-axis. | [[☃ dropdown 2]]|

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The Quadrilateral A B C D has point A at negative one, negative one, point B at zero, three, point C at two, one, and point D at two, zero. A point P is at negative four, negative three.
